title: Make idle shell close readiness reliable
summary: The Tauri shell retries one transient loopback close-readiness transport failure before showing the force-close prompt.
reason: An idle shell could show a force-close prompt after a temporary local backend connection failure even though the backend had no active work.
behavior_before: One failed GET /api/backend/close-readiness request immediately showed the unsafe-close confirmation dialog.
behavior_after: The shell waits 150 ms and retries the close-readiness transport request once; a verified unsafe payload or malformed payload is never retried or treated as safe.
manual_validation: git diff --check on change packet paths - passed
ops/scripts/release/test.ps1 -SkipToolIntegration -SkipEndToEndSmoke - timed out after 64 seconds without output
rollback_plan: Revert the close_readiness.rs retry constants, retry loop, and associated focused tests to restore one-attempt close-readiness behavior.
notes:
Retry one transient loopback close-readiness transport failure before showing the unsafe-close prompt; unsafe backend payloads remain authoritative.
Rust unit coverage for one transient close-readiness transport failure is embedded with the shell close-readiness module; scaffold remains the affected Tauri lifecycle coverage entry point.
Focused Rust transport-retry and static shell-structure checks pass. Full existing Tauri test groups have unrelated WebView fixture and route-contract drift failures in the dirty workspace.
Repository-level release self-test was started but did not complete within the bounded 64-second window; it was terminated without output.
